Q.2 [1 Mark]
The President, along with the Council of Ministers, ___________ to visit India next
week.
Select the most appropriate option to complete the above sentence.
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: Let's analyze the grammatical rule of Subject-Verb Agreement: • When a subject is joined with other nouns using prepositional phrases such as "along with", "as well as", "together with", "in addition to", the verb must agree in person and number with the primary (first) subject, NOT with the nouns inside the parenthetical phrase. • Here, the primary subject is "The President" (Third-person singular). • Therefore, the verb must be singular: "wishes". • Additionally, the verb "wish" is a stative verb expressing desire or intent, so the simple present form wishes is standard rather than continuous is wishing. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (A): wish - Plural verb form; incorrect because "The President" is singular. • Option (C): will wish - Future tense of a stative intention verb is awkward and grammatically unnatural here. • Option (D): is wishing - Stative verbs of wanting/intending are typically not used in continuous aspect.
